answer: I would grant each archive key one daily vote only after it holds a distinct 1 GiB key-sealed replica of ridge and terrace lantern logs for 24 hours. Validators check replication proofs and random timed storage challenges; failed or missing proofs deny the vote. More keys require more replicas, even on shared disks: n keys occupy n GiB all day. Disks are reusable capital; rental and power recur. This assumes proofs prevent deduplication and cheap regeneration, not merely receipt reuse. Wealthy operators can still buy influence.
